sentences.text: The history of Earth concerns the development of the planet Earth from its formation to the present day .	Earth	Earth
Nearly all branches of natural science have contributed to the understanding of the main events of the Earth 's past .	Earth	Earth	natural science	natural science
The age of Earth is approximately one-third of the age of the universe .	Earth	Earth	age of Earth	Age of the Earth	age of the universe	age of the universe	universe	universe
An immense amount of geological change has occurred in that timespan , accompanied by the emergence of life and its subsequent evolution .	geological	geology	life	life	evolution	evolution
Earth formed around 4.54 billion years ago by accretion from the solar nebula .	Earth	Earth	accretion	accretion (astrophysics)	solar nebula	solar nebula

Volcanic outgassing probably created the primordial atmosphere and then the ocean ; but the atmosphere contained almost no oxygen and so would have been toxic to most modern life including humans .	life	life	outgassing	outgassing	oxygen	oxygen
Much of the Earth was molten because of frequent collisions with other bodies which led to extreme volcanism .	Earth	Earth

A giant impact collision with a planet-sized body named Theia while Earth was in its earliest stage , also known as Early Earth , is thought to have been responsible for forming the Moon .	Earth	Earth	Theia	Theia (planet)	Early Earth	Early Earth
Over time , the Earth cooled , causing the formation of a solid crust , and allowing liquid water to exist on the surface .	Earth	Earth	crust	crust (geology)

The geological time scale -LRB- GTS -RRB- clock -LRB- see graphic -RRB- depicts the larger spans of time from the beginning of the Earth as well as a chronology of some definitive events of Earth history .	Earth	Earth	geological	geology

The Hadean Eon represents time before the reliable -LRB- fossil -RRB- record of life beginning on Earth ; it began with the formation of the planet and ended at 4.0 billion years ago as defined by international convention .	Earth	Earth	life	life	Hadean	Hadean	Eon	Geologic time scale	fossil	fossil
The Archean and Proterozoic eons follow ; they produced the abiogenesis of life on Earth and then the evolution of early life .	Earth	Earth	life	life	evolution	evolution	abiogenesis	abiogenesis

The succeeding eon is the Phanerozoic , which is represented by its three component eras : the Palaeozoic ; the Mesozoic , which spanned the rise , reign , and climactic extinction of the huge dinosaurs ; and the Cenozoic , which presented the subsequent development of dominant mammals on Earth .	Earth	Earth	Cenozoic	Cenozoic

Hominins , the earliest direct ancestors of the human clade , rose sometime during the latter part of the Miocene epoch ; the precise time marking the first hominins is broadly debated over a current range of 13 to 4 mya .	Hominins	Hominins	Miocene	Miocene	first hominins	CHLCA

The succeeding Quaternary period is the time of recognizable humans , i.e. , the genus Homo , but that period 's two million-year-plus term of the recent times is too small to be visible at the scale of the GTS graphic .	Quaternary	Quaternary	Homo	Homo
-LRB- Notes re the graphic : Ga means `` billion years '' ; Ma , `` million years '' . -RRB-	Ga	Year#Abbreviations yr and ya	Ma	Year#Abbreviations yr and ya

The earliest undisputed evidence of life on Earth dates at least from 3.5 billion years ago , during the Eoarchean Era after a geological crust started to solidify following the earlier molten Hadean Eon .	Earth	Earth	geological	geology	life	life	crust	crust (geology)	Eoarchean	Eoarchean	Hadean	Hadean	Eon	Geologic time scale

There are microbial mat fossils such as stromatolites found in 3.48 billion-year-old sandstone discovered in Western Australia .	microbial mat	microbial mat	stromatolites	stromatolites	sandstone	sandstone	Western Australia	Western Australia

Other early physical evidence of a biogenic substance is graphite in 3.7 billion-year-old metasedimentary rocks discovered in southwestern Greenland as well as `` remains of biotic life '' found in 4.1 billion-year-old rocks in Western Australia .	life	life	Western Australia	Western Australia	biogenic substance	biogenic substance	graphite	graphite	metasedimentary rocks	Metasediment	Greenland	Greenland	biotic life	Biotic material
According to one of the researchers , `` If life arose relatively quickly on Earth ... then it could be common in the universe . ''	Earth	Earth	life	life	universe	universe
Living forms derived from photosynthesis appeared between 3.2 and 2.4 billion years ago and began enriching the atmosphere with oxygen .	oxygen	oxygen	photosynthesis	photosynthesis

Life remained mostly small and microscopic until about 580 million years ago , when complex multicellular life arose , developed over time , and culminated in the Cambrian Explosion about 541 million years ago .	life	life	Life	Life	580 million years ago	Timeline of human evolution#First living beings	multicellular life	multicellular organism	Cambrian Explosion	Cambrian Explosion

This event drove a rapid diversification of life forms on Earth that produced most of the major phyla known today ; and it marked the end of the Proterozoic Eon and the beginning of the Cambrian Period of the Paleozoic Era .	Earth	Earth	life	life	Eon	Geologic time scale
More than 99 percent of all species , amounting to over five billion species , that ever lived on Earth are estimated to be extinct .	Earth	Earth	extinct	Extinction	species	species

Estimates on the number of Earth 's current species range from 10 million to 14 million , of which about 1.2 million have been documented and over 86 percent have not yet been described .	Earth	Earth	species	species
More recently , in May 2016 , scientists reported that 1 trillion species are estimated to be on Earth currently with only one-thousandth of one percent described .	Earth	Earth	species	species
Geological change has been a constant of Earth 's crust since the time of its formation , and biological change since the first appearance of life .	Earth	Earth	life	life	crust	crust (geology)

Species continue to evolve , taking on new forms , splitting into daughter species or going extinct in the process of adapting or dying in response to ever-changing physical environments .	extinct	Extinction	species	species	evolve	evolution

The process of plate tectonics continues to play a dominant role in the shaping of Earth 's oceans and continents and the living species they harbor .	Earth	Earth	species	species	plate tectonics	plate tectonics

Changes in the biosphere -- now dominated by human activity -- continue , in turn , to produce significant effects on the atmosphere and other systems of the Earth 's surface , such as the integrity of the ozone layer , the proliferation of greenhouse gases , the conditions of productive soils and clean air and water , and others .	Earth	Earth	biosphere	biosphere	ozone layer	ozone layer	greenhouse gases	greenhouse gases
